image_description: A close-up, slightly angled shot of a metal shelving unit densely packed with audio cassette tapes. The cassettes are arranged vertically, showing their spines which feature various colors, logos, and text (band names like Radiohead, Queensryche, Iron Maiden). To the left, there is a spiral-bound notebook and a green plastic bag. The lighting appears to be indoor ambient light, casting soft shadows between the cases.

artifact_observations.location: Spine labels of multiple cassettes, particularly in the middle and right sections of the shelves.
artifact_observations.reasoning: While major band names are legible, many smaller text elements and secondary titles exhibit slight character fusion, irregular kerning, or nonsensical letter combinations typical of AI text generation. Some logos appear slightly distorted or morphed.

artifact_observations.location: Left edge of the image, specifically the interface between the spiral notebook and the green bag.
artifact_observations.reasoning: The red spiral binding of the notebook seems to merge indistinctly with the background and the green bag lacks clear structural definition, appearing somewhat 'melted' or amorphous compared to the rigid cassettes.

artifact_observations.location: Vertical alignment of cassettes on the middle shelf.
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight waviness in the vertical lines of the cassette spines suggests minor geometric inconsistency, though it could also be attributed to physical warping of old cases. It is subtle but noticeable upon close inspection.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the objects are indeed audio cassettes and not similar rectangular media cases (like VHS or DVD) given the spine-only view.
To rigorously evaluate the legibility and correctness of the printed text, which is a primary source of artifacts in this image.
To check for boundary bleeding between the tightly packed cassettes and ensure each case is a distinct, separate object.
To assess the lighting consistency and texture realism of the plastic surfaces versus the paper labels.
